justification: A puts every failing rule, its code, and its status inline at flat guard-clause endpoints (e.g. if (order is null) return Results.Problem($"order-not-found:{id}", statusCode: 409)), so failures and absence read at a glance with plain ASP.NET Core Results. B's typed closed error hierarchies and clean rules-vs-HTTP layering are well commented, but control flow routes through Validation/Option/Result combinators (Zip, Traverse, Ensure, ToHttpResult) across two files, so connecting a failure to its cause and status requires knowing library semantics and hopping between files.
